-----
Coram Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rajesh Shankar

----- 
 For the Petitioners: Mr. Ramchander Sahu
 For the State: Mr. Sanjay Kumar Tiwari, S.C-I

For the Nhai: Ms. Sweety Topno
 -----

The present writ petition has been filed for issuance of direction upo
respondents for payment of appropriate compensation along with interest to the petitioners in lieu
of acquisition of their land as well as the structure standing over the same situated at Khata No. 2,
Plot No. 1142, Village-Ujjaina, Thana No. 70, P.S-Barhi, District-Hazaribagh, measuring an area of
0.02000 acre out of total area of 0.0700 acre (07 decimals) concerning Award No. 105 prepared in
L. A. Case No. 29/2013-14 initiated for widening of Nh-31 treating the same to be commercial land
in place of agricultural land as compensation for acquisition of the adjacent land has been fixed at
the commercial rate.
Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the said land was recorded in the name of the petitioner's grandfather-Khirodhar Teli in the cadastral survey.

Though the respondent No.3 acquired 0.0200 Acre (02 decimals) of the said land for widening of NH-31, however, the award was prepared only to the extent of 0.01000 Acre (01 decimal) in the name of Ritlal Teli @ Ritlal Sao, son Triveni Sao vs The State Of Jharkhand on 13 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28839450/
1 of Late Khirodhar Teli @ Khirodhar Sao.

entities.text: Triveni Sao vs The State Of Jharkhand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Ritlal Sao died on 19.07.2019 and thereafter the petitioners being his legal heirs have lawful right over the said land.

The main grievance of the petitioners is that the award for acquisition of the said land has been prepared on agricultural rate that too for 0.01000 acre whereas the same has been prepared on commercial rate for acquisition of the adjacent land.

Mr. Sanjay Kumar Tiwari, learned S.C-I appearing on behalf of the State- respondents as well as Ms.
Sweety Topno, learned counsel for the respondent- NHAI, jointly raise a preliminary objection with regard to maintainability of the present writ petition on the ground that the petitioners have got an alternative/statutory/efficacious remedy of preferring an application under Section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956 [hereinafter referred to as 'the Act, 1956'] before the Additional Collector-cum-Arbitrator, Hazaribagh under the Act, 1956 against the quantum of compensation fixed in the said award.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and keeping in view that the petitioners have got an alternative/statutory/efficacious remedy of preferring an application under Section 3G(5) of the Act,
1956 before the Additional Collector- cum-Arbitrator, Hazaribagh under the Act, 1956 against the quantum of compensation fixed in the said award, I am not inclined to entertain the present writ petition on merit and the same is accordingly dismissed as not maintainable.
The petitioners are however at liberty to take recourse of Section 3G(5) of the Act, 1956 for redressal of their grievance.

Satish/- (RAJESH SHANKAR, J)
